cards.title: What are articles?
cards.body: a, an, the — small words before nouns. Czech has none at all, which is why articles are the number-one English problem for Czech speakers, at every level. They are not optional: almost every singular noun needs one.
cards.body_cz: a, an, the — malá slova před podstatnými jmény. Čeština žádné nemá — proto jsou členy problém č. 1 pro české mluvčí na všech úrovních. Nejsou volitelné.

cards.title: What do they do?
cards.body: They tell the listener which thing you mean. a dog = any dog, one of many, new information. the dog = you both know which one. No article = things in general (Dogs are friendly).
cards.body_cz: Říkají posluchači, o kterou věc jde. a dog = nějaký pes (nový). the dog = ten pes (oba víme který). Bez členu = obecně (Dogs are friendly).

cards.title: Why does English need them?
cards.body: Czech signals known vs new by word order and endings. English word order is fixed, so articles carry that signal instead. Skip them and the listener loses track of what's new and what's known.
cards.body_cz: Čeština ukazuje známé vs nové slovosledem a koncovkami. Angličtina má pevný slovosled — tuhle práci dělají členy. Bez nich se posluchač ztrácí.

cards.body: in hospital / at school / at work = the activity. the hospital = the building.
